quote: The outputs of text generation systems are increasingly seen as human-like...
To probe which types of LLM-generated outputs (system behaviors) participants might deem to be human-like, and how they would rewrite those outputs to make them less human-like...
outputs: Generated responses to user inputs in conversational settings
The paper studies anthropomorphic behaviors in text generated by LLMs in conversational settings and interventions to make such outputs less human-like.

quote: we designed a crowdsourcing study to surface additional possible interventions. This study was IRB-approved, and consent was obtained from each participant before participation... Participants were then asked to highlight the words or phrases in the output text that seem human-like to them... rated how human-like the text appears to them on a five-point scale... identified why the text appears human-like to them by selecting from a multiple-choice list...

We designed our study to probe which types of LLM-generated outputs ... participants were asked to read the text the system generated ... they 1) rated how human-like the text appears to them on a five-point scale, and 2) identified why the text appears human-like ... Finally, they were asked to rewrite the text to be NOT human-like or less human-like.

We recruited a total of 350 US-based, English-speaking participants on Prolific, with each participant completing a single task that included four different examples (pairs of user input and generated responses).
guideline: Participants rated human-likeness on a five-point scale and selected reasons from predefined anthropomorphic behavior categories, then rewrote the text to be less human-like.

Participants rated the human-likeness of each output on a five-point scale, selected the perceived anthropomorphic behaviors from a predefined list, provided open-ended explanations, and rewrote the output to reduce human-like qualities.

Participants were asked to highlight words or phrases that seem human-like, rate how human-like the text appears on a five-point scale, select why the text appears human-like from a multiple-choice list, answer an open-ended question about other human-like qualities, and rewrite the text to be less human-like.
